pcb_frame.note: pcb_outline, components and key_board are in the KiCad board frame (the frame of the first v0.7 layout, a 94.4 mm body): housing X = board X + 2.75. Everything else in this file is in the housing frame (X = 0 at the front face of the 99.2 mm body).

J1_usb.note: TYPE-C-31-M-12 on the bottom side, mating face flush with the PCB edge

buttons.note: v0.7: the three switches sit on the bottom face of the key board (KB), actuator pointing down at the keys; rot 0 = the two pads along housing X, rot 90 = pads along housing Y. The main board does not carry them any more.

ring_leds.note: emit downwards into the top face of the clear main key (key top Z 2.90 at rest, LED face Z 3.50 for the 0.85 mm worst-case LED height)

S2_interlock.note: PCM12-class slide, knob towards +Y into the wall slot

U4_module.note: ESP32-C3-MINI-1, antenna overhangs the rear edge by 5.4 mm

keepout_top.note: no top-side components inside; copper, vias and solder mask allowed

components.max_height_top_note: under the lid plate; within 0.64 of the board edges (|Y| > 7.61) the lid's inner edge limits the parts to Z 14.40 (4.40 above the board)

kb_zone.note: bottom-side parts of the main board above the key board must clear the KB top-face parts (pogo barrels, screw heads, resistors); J6 target pads right above the pogo pins

key_board.screw: M1.6 x 2.5 pan head, stainless steel

rf_windows.window material: POM-C black (both); between X 36.35 and 41.45 no metal above or below the module from Y -5.4 to 5.2; its -Y edge strip (Y -8 to -5.4) has aluminium round it (floor corner, side wall, lid seat and diagonal wall)

pogo_stack.note: spring force linear through the free height (1.17 N at 4.00 mm)

key_tolerance_stack.note: a negative value is a preload on the switch: for the elastomer keys it is taken by the rubber (a few tenths of a newton per 0.1 mm), for the rigid PMMA key only the worst case (all tolerances at their limit at once) goes below zero, and still stays below the click (about 0.20 mm)

side_key_chevron.previous_key: X 32.65: apex towards the tail (+X), the same part turned 180 deg
side_key_chevron.reading: held like a presenter (head towards the screen, keys up): the key nearest the head reads '^' (next), the key nearest the hand 'v' (previous)

FlashKa_pom_kit.not_in_the_kit: laser sleeve (option, only for a laser module thinner than 6 mm): its slit along the axis needs a side setup; single file FlashKa_laser_sleeve.step
FlashKa_pom_kit.setups: top (kit +Z): insert faces with the texture, spacer floor plug with the texture and its bottom chamfers; bottom: insert flange undersides, spacer top side (U, rebate, tall wall); the gaps from each side to the tab plane

laser_retention.screw: M1.6 x 5 set screw, ISO 4026 flat point or ISO 4029 cup point, hex socket, stainless steel
laser_retention.entry: from the head-block top (Z 14.6), under the front end of the lid; fitted with the lid off
laser_retention.thread: M1.6x0.35-6H, tap drill d1.25 from the head-block top into the laser bore

optic_seat.optic: LEDiL LISA3-RS-PIN (FP16558): d10.0, 6.93 +/-0.2 above the LED board (LEDiL drawing FP165xx LISA3-x-PIN rev 1.2; data sheet 6.9), PMMA lens in a black PC holder; the two pins are cut off
optic_seat.seat: the holder base stands on the front face of the LED board (the LED level, as LEDiL designs it: 'PCB or heatsink level. LED location'); the LED board lies on the bore floor with thermal paste; no spacer, no window
optic_seat.vignetting: the bore keeps its full diameter to the front face (no lip, no window): from the edge of the exit (r 4.30) a ray clears the bore mouth (r 5.050) up to 61.9 deg from the axis at the deepest seat (recess 0.4), 75.1 deg at the nominal one
optic_seat.retention: two-part epoxy (or neutral-cure silicone) on the holder rim against the bore wall, the optic pressed onto the LED board while it cures; no cyanoacrylate (its vapour fogs PMMA).  Not a press fit: the thin PC holder would have to carry the fit, the bore is +0.05/0, and the LED board must stay pressed onto the floor.  The glued optic traps the LED board on the bore floor.
optic_seat.led_wires: the pads face the two wire grooves (upper groove 30 deg from 12 o'clock towards the laser, lower one opposite); if the holder base sits on the solder joints, file two notches into the holder rim

bay.bay_section: inside of the octagon: 17 wide between the side walls, floor Z 1.5, lid plate Z 16.5; 45 deg corners (lower -Y corner = channel for the joints and the far-end wire)

rails.insulation: polyimide tape 0.05 on each rail; the cell keeps its own sleeve

bay.length_budget: 51.6 = longest cell 50.4 + 2 x 0.4 (nickel strip 0.2 + fold / weld bumps) + 0.4 (tail pad at its thinnest)
bay.holding: the cell rests on the two rails (it cannot roll); a soft closed-cell foam strip 6 wide under the lid presses it down and a foam pad at the tail end takes up the length; both are stacks of 0.5 mm foam sheet, each about 1.6 x the gap it fills (compressed 20 to 55 %, see the cases); F15 nominal: 1.5 mm strip, 3 mm tail pad
bay.connection: nickel strips (0.2 x 5) spot-welded to both ends (pre-tabbed cell or a spot welder; never solder on the can); front end = BAT+ (cell + towards the head): its strip is bent forward into the antenna-spacer rebate and the 24 AWG wire soldered to it there; far end = BAT-: its strip is bent into the lower -Y corner channel, the wire soldered there runs forward in the channel
bay.heat_path: the cell touches the body only along the two rails (through the tape) and through the foam: weakly coupled; no thermal pad (a gap pad pressed over the cell length would load the lid with tens of newtons)

wire_paths.led_holes_on_the_groove_line: hole axis r 5.70 from the optic axis = groove channel centre (r 5.000 .. 6.350): the wire runs straight, none passes under the LED board
wire_paths.laser_wires: 28 AWG, unchanged (beside the laser module under the main board)

led_to_key_gap.note: gap at full travel = switch height - travel - LED height - (key top to nub depth): independent of the floor and the KB height; a lower real LED only makes both gaps larger
